brief: A seven-cell honeycomb work surface, covered on top, with every open outside edge finished with caps.

requirements.requirement: Seven-cell honeycomb work surface (centre cell plus six around it)
requirements.evidence: Seven Hex base · Full pieces at axial (0,0), (1,0), (1,-1), (0,-1), (-1,0), (-1,1), (0,1), all on level 0. check_build reports no issues and meshClash clear.
Seven full top covers (cover:...;full;top) on every base cell.

requirements.requirement: Every open outside edge finished with caps
requirements.evidence: capOpenFaces added 18 solid end caps on the exterior faces of the outer ring; lockJoints added 12 joint bolts. No open faces remain per the house-rule op.

finish.summary: Built a seven-cell flower-shaped honeycomb work surface: seven full hex bases on one level, each with a top cover, with the outside edges closed by 18 solid caps and the joints locked with 12 bolts. check_build is clean (no issues, meshClash clear). I did not add props, since the brief did not ask for a use-dressed setup. Material and load suitability are not verified by the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
